subject: RTBF coordination: deletion flow matrix & backup exemptions
messages:

Cc: Orchid Labs Legal <legal@orchidlabs.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo questions: RTBF / backups / residency

Thanks for the demo today — useful to see the latency and cost profiles. A few privacy-ops items we need to lock down before the pilot: 

- Scope of PII in the platform: which artifacts are considered "customer PII" vs derived embeddings/logs. We need to map exactly what Redwood will delete on request.
- Deletion timeline expectations: we heard ~48-72h for active storage, but unclear re: backups/snapshots and immutable archives. Are there known exceptions?
- Logging & telemetry: audit logs, request traces, and analytics — can these be purged or pseudonymized?
- Data residency: our EU product will require EU-only data at rest; how does RTBF interact with cross-region backups?

I've attached an initial RTBF matrix we maintain (orchid_rtbf_matrix.xlsx) with our current asks. Can you confirm which items are supported today, which are "on roadmap," and which are not possible due to backup/replication constraints?

Also looping in Legal for any contractual redlines (cc'd). 

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Hart
Head of Security & Privacy
Orchid Labs

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Mike Hart <mike.hart@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RTBF coordination: deletion flow matrix & backup exemptions

Mike — great questions, and thanks for the spreadsheet. I've reviewed your matrix and sketched a pragmatic remediation path we can deliver for a pilot. High-level notes below; Ben (cc) will follow up with the technical mapping.

1) What Redwood deletes on a standard RTBF: user content (messages, uploaded files), indexed metadata, and embeddings generated from customer inputs. We do not include system-level telemetry needed for platform integrity unless specifically requested and approved.

2) Timeline expectations: standard purge from active stores: 24–72 hours after request confirmation. Backups: most cloud snapshot systems are immutable for a retention window; we offer two paths — (A) time-based expiry aligned to your retention policy (we can set shorter retention for your account under Dedicated/Private), or (B) targeted restore-and-purge: we can restore a snapshot, reapply a delete, and re-snapshot — this adds operational time (typically 7–30 days depending on snapshot size and legal holds).

3) Logs & telemetry: audit logs are kept for 90 days by default; we can provide export or pseudonymization on a per-contract basis. Full deletion of platform telemetry is possible for Dedicated/Private with pre-agreed config; for Hosted customers there are constraints tied to observability tooling and incident response requirements.

4) Residency implications: if data is pinned to the EU region, backups are likewise placed in-region by default. Cross-region replication is opt-in. For Orchid's EU product we can ensure in-region snapshot retention, which simplifies RTBF compliance.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben will produce a deletion-action matrix mapping each Orchid artifact to Redwood systems and an estimated completion window.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute technical call to run through the matrix and agree on a pilot deletion (canary purge).
- We'll share a draft contractual clause for backups/retention to put in your SOW.

Attaching a short Redwood delete SLA summary for reference (redwood_delete-sla.pdf). Let me know if you want us to prioritize any specific artifact for the pilot.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_delete-sla.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Hart <mike.hart@orchidlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RTBF coordination: deletion flow matrix & backup exemptions

Following up with the technical mapping we discussed on the call. Summary notes and constraints below; full matrix attached (deletion-action-matrix.csv).

- Active stores: user blobs, embeddings, and index shards can be zeroed and GC'd; estimate 24–48h for small accounts (<1TB), 48–72h for larger.
- KV caches / inference caches: per-token caches are ephemeral; clearing KV cache invalidates future responses immediately. We can force cache flush during a purge.
- Snapshot/backups: cloud snapshots are immutable until TTL expiry. For Hosted: default snapshot retention 30 days; for Dedicated we can configure to 7/30/90 days per contract. Immediate removal requires restoration -> delete -> new snapshot flow. Restoration time dominates (depends on data size and IO limits).
- Audit logs: stored in a separate logging cluster with roll-forward replication. We can pseudonymize within 7 days; full deletion requires log-compaction which is scheduled monthly.
- Legal holds & eDiscovery: if a hold is active, deletion will be paused; we'll surface the hold in the deletion workflow and provide evidence for your legal team.

I've attached the CSV matrix that lists each artifact (column A), system owner (col B), default retention, and required SOW change to enable immediate purge. Please review and mark three artifacts you'd like to include in the pilot.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: deletion-action-matrix.csv (text/csv)
